newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Mining to build port in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Mining to build port in Vietnam.

text.p: Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd (MMC) and a Singapore company will jointly develop a new $500 million port in south Vietnam, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.

The Vietnamese Ministry of Planning and Investment's Foreign Investment Department vice-director Tran Quan Ngoc was quoted by Bernama as saying that MMC was conducting a feasibility study on the project on which work was expected to start by end-1997.
The Sao Mai Port will be part of a three-phase development of the Thivai River spanning a period of 20 years, Tran told reporters at a Malaysia-Vietnam business seminar.
"Currently, we are using Saigon Port and once the Sao Mai Port development is completed, everything will be shifted there and Saigon Port will only be used for domestic shipment," Tran said.
Sao Mai Port will have a cargo handling capacity of 100 million tonnes a year compared with only nine million tonnes at Saigon Port at present, he said.
Tran did not name the Singapore company.
